claims.text: In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a "small business" means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000.

In the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a "small company" means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

"Gross turnover" means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants.
In deciding whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company for value added tax returns, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded.
The value of a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business is also excluded.
The requirement to file value added tax returns under section 22(1) does not apply to a small business.

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns.
A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns.

In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a "small business" means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

In the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a "small company" means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

"Gross turnover" means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

In deciding whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company for value added tax returns, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The value of a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business is also excluded. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The requirement to file value added tax returns under section 22(1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

- The passages do not state which turnover limit applies to a particular business, and any comparison of a business's turnover with the limits is not done here.

Sources

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-references: subsection (4), sections 105 and 107 (cited) against subsection (5), sections 100 and 102 (National Assembly). (DR-198)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-reference: section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act (cited) against section 151 (National Assembly text, the same section under its numbering, DR-000). (DR-199)

claims.text: A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form, with or without a notice and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, on or before the 21st day of the following month.
The VAT return must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable on all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
The 21st-day filing rule in subsection (1) does not apply to a small business.

A small business may, by written notice to the Service, choose to opt out of the small business exemption, including registration, charging tax on taxable supplies and filing returns. This choice does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
A business that stops being a small business must file monthly VAT returns.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person must render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.
If the Service extends the time for filing a VAT return, that extension does not extend the time to pay the tax.

A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues.
Any balance of tax unpaid as at the due date attracts interest and penalties as provided in the Act or any other relevant law.

cases.question: I filed my company's VAT return three months late. What is the total penalty?

claims.text: A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs.

A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of tax payable is added to it, subject to section 67 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Interest also runs on unpaid tax from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. For naira remittances, the rate is the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread to be determined by the Minister. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

For foreign currency remittances, unpaid tax carries interest at the prevailing Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say which provision covers a VAT return specifically, or whether the general failure-to-file penalty applies to a VAT return.
- The question needs a calculation of the total for three months of late filing. The passages do not give a total and no calculation is done here.
- The passages do not say whether the return was filed late with tax unpaid, so it is unclear whether the non-payment penalty and interest apply.
- Section 67 of the Act, to which the non-payment penalty is subject, is not among the passages.
- The Minister's spread for naira interest is not stated in the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101 (gazette page A 312)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65 (gazette pages A 298, A 299)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Interest is SOFR plus 10% or such other spread as the authority determines in the cited text; the National Assembly text says SOFR plus a spread to be determined, without the 10%. (DR-243)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Only the cited text makes the interest in subsection (1)(b) and (c) compound and applies it to tax debts unpaid at commencement. (DR-245)

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. - Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)

(DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s72 subsections (2) to (4): banks and government bodies demand a certificate for the three years before the current year of assessment for the listed transactions.
cases.question: Why would my bank ask for a tax clearance certificate, and how many years must it cover?

claims.text: Any commercial bank with which a person has any dealing in respect of the transactions listed in subsection (4) shall demand from that person a tax clearance certificate of three years immediately preceding the current year of assessment.

The listed transactions are: application for certificate of occupancy, approval of building plans, application for award of contract by government or its agencies, application for firearms licence, application for import and export licence, and application for trade licence.

A tax clearance certificate shall disclose, for the last three years of assessment, total profits or chargeable income, tax payable, tax paid, and tax outstanding or alternatively a statement that no tax is due.

The relevant tax authority shall issue a tax clearance certificate within two weeks of the demand where it is of the opinion that tax assessed has been fully paid or that no tax is due, or else give reasons for the denial.

gaps: The passages do not say which of the listed transactions, if any, apply to the person's particular dealing with the bank, such as a loan or account opening.

claims.text: Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Taxpayer Identification ("Tax ID") for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations.

The same person is liable to pay ₦25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues.
A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for a Tax ID but failed to do so.
The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID.
A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government.
A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000.

A Tax ID must be stated on a return, notice, correspondence or documents submitted, lodged or used for tax compliance, and on a document prepared, produced, issued or submitted in respect of a transaction.
A person engaged in banking, insurance, stock-broking or other financial services in Nigeria shall ensure that every taxable person provides a Tax ID.

cases.rendered:
Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Taxpayer Identification ("Tax ID") for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax under section 4 is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

The same person is liable to pay ₦25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for a Tax ID but failed to do so. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A Tax ID must be stated on a return, notice, correspondence or documents submitted, lodged or used for tax compliance, and on a document prepared, produced, issued or submitted in respect of a transaction. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

A person engaged in banking, insurance, stock-broking or other financial services in Nigeria shall ensure that every taxable person provides a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the company is a taxable person is not stated in the passages and depends on its facts.
- The total penalty for a given number of months needs a calculation, which is not done here.
- Any other consequences of not registering, such as for tax owed or enforcement, are not in the passages.

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8: The cited text requires financial institutions to ensure every taxable person provides a Tax ID; the National Assembly text makes a Tax ID a precondition for opening or operating any account. (DR-186)

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, and for a small company the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, it shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%, notwithstanding any provision of the Act or any other enactment. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is listed as qualifying capital expenditure (qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure).
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, which has a rate of 20%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance at the Table I rate is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which that asset was used for that trade or business.
A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person owns the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.

The 1% of qualifying capital expenditure recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes is a notional amount and does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable.

The residue of a qualifying expenditure at a date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date.

An allowance shall not be made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
Where an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it shall be carried forward to a subsequent period.

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the relevant year. Where there is no remainder or an insufficient remainder, the deduction, or the part not yet made, is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised.

gaps: The yearly amount needs a calculation of the rate on the expenditure, which is not done here.
Whether the allowance is applied to the original cost or to the residue each year is not stated in the passages, so the yearly amounts after the first cannot be set out.
Whether the furniture is used wholly for the business, and whether the buyer is a company, are not stated in the question.

Where an owner partly uses an asset for a trade or business, the allowance is apportioned to the trade or business as may be reasonable, and the relevant tax authority may make adjustments if it considers the basis of apportionment not just and reasonable.

cases.rationale: nta2025:s156 subsection (1)(a): where output VAT exceeds input VAT, the excess is remitted; the difference must not be computed.
cases.question: Our input VAT this month is ₦1.8 million and our output VAT is ₦2.5 million. How much do we pay?

claims.text: A taxable person must, not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, remit the excess to the Service where output VAT exceeds input VAT.
Where input VAT exceeds output VAT instead, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess as a credit against subsequent months.
Input VAT is the VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person.
Output VAT is the VAT a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies.

A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month, and the return must show the input tax paid, output tax collected and VAT payable for the preceding month.
If the Service grants an extension of the time for filing returns, that does not extend the time to pay the tax.

Input tax may be deducted only to the extent that it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies. Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to taxable supplies may be deducted.
The VAT return filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business.

gaps: The amount payable needs a subtraction of input VAT from output VAT, which is not done here.
The passages do not say whether all of the input VAT in the question is deductible, for example whether it relates wholly to taxable supplies.

cases.question: My company sells furniture, has turnover of about ₦30 million a year and fixed assets worth ₦40 million. What company income tax rate applies to it?

claims.text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%.
Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.
A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
A business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

A company with an effective tax rate below 15% must recompute and pay additional tax to reach 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

gaps: Whether the company's furniture business counts as providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
Whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group is not stated.

Whether the company's turnover and fixed assets are gross turnover per annum and total fixed assets as the definition uses them is not stated; the comparison of the figures with the thresholds is left to the reader.

My company sells furniture, has turnover of about ₦30 million a year and fixed assets worth ₦40 million. What company income tax rate applies to it?
</question>

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A company with an effective tax rate below 15% must recompute and pay additional tax to reach 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the company's furniture business counts as providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
- Whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group is not stated.
- Whether the company's turnover and fixed assets are gross turnover per annum and total fixed assets as the definition uses them is not stated; the comparison of the figures with the thresholds is left to the reader.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s73(1)-(4): advance rulings on application by a taxable person, issued within 21 days or with written reasons.
cases.question: Can my company ask the tax service for a written ruling on how a law applies before we go ahead with a deal?

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as it does not amend or replace the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling upon application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give written reasons for being unable to issue it.
An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to any tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to one.

The definition of advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision issued to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.

An application must contain the taxpayer's contact details, a complete description of the tax issue or transaction and its financial implications if any, and a complete description of the impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person.

An application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether or not the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.
The tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, or an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious.

The tax authority may also reject an application where the ruling will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or persons connected to the applicant.
A ruling's effect is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, and it is rendered on a set of facts before the tax authority and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction described is materially different from the one actually carried out, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law it concerned is repealed or amended in a manner that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based.

gaps: The passages do not say that a company is a taxable person or a person who may apply; the definition of company is given but no passage links it to the application rules.
The passages do not say which body is the relevant tax authority for a particular tax.
The prescribed form and manner of application is not set out in the passages.

Where a trade, business, profession or vocation permanently ceases to carry on operations in Nigeria in an accounting period, the tax is payable within six months from the date of cessation.

cases.rendered:
Every person shall pay tax due on or before the due date of filing, in one lump sum or in instalments, and the final instalment shall be paid on or before the due date of filing. This is subject to section 11 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Tax charged by an assessment that is not or has not been the subject of an objection or appeal is payable within 30 days of service of the notice of assessment on the taxable person, after deducting any set-off amount or amount deposited against the tax. The relevant tax authority, in its discretion, may extend the time for payment. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Where notice of an objection or appeal has been given, collection of the tax stays in abeyance until it is determined, subject to section 11 of the Act, but the taxable person shall pay the tax that is not the subject of the objection or appeal. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

After an objection or appeal is determined, the tax authority serves a notice of the tax payable, and that tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of that notice. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Where tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the tax payable is added, and interest runs from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. This is subject to section 67 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The tax authority serves a demand notice on the company or person in whose name tax is chargeable. If payment is not made within 30 days from the date of service of the demand notice, the tax authority may proceed to enforce payment. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Where a trade, business, profession or vocation permanently ceases to carry on operations in Nigeria in an accounting period, the tax is payable within six months from the date of cessation. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 24]

If an extension of time to pay is granted and the person fails to pay within the extended period, penalty and interest accrue from the original due date as if no extension was granted. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The question does not say which tax or situation it means, so the matching time limit cannot be picked.
- Section 11 of the Act, which section 49 refers to, is not among the passages.
- Section 67, which section 65 refers to, is not among the passages.
- The period prescribed under the Act for payment, which section 65 refers to, is not stated in section 65 itself.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6) (gazette pages A 288, A 289)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65 (gazette pages A 298, A 299)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 24 (gazette pages A 411, A 412)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Interest is SOFR plus 10% or such other spread as the authority determines in the cited text; the National Assembly text says SOFR plus a spread to be determined, without the 10%. (DR-243)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Only the cited text makes the interest in subsection (1)(b) and (c) compound and applies it to tax debts unpaid at commencement. (DR-245)

A VAT invoice must show the VAT charged and the rate, along with the gross amount of the transaction. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 153]

- The amount of VAT on the invoices needs a calculation (applying the rate to the sales value), which is not done here.

claims.text: All forms of property, including shares, are chargeable assets for the purpose of this Part, whether situated in Nigeria or not, subject to exemptions provided in Part I of Chapter Eight of the Act.

Gains accruing to a person on disposal of shares in any Nigerian company shall not be chargeable gains where the disposal proceeds, in aggregate, are less than ₦150,000,000 and the chargeable gain does not exceed ₦10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months.

A company may be charged to tax in its own name.

must_not: claim that disclosure is needed only when the tax office asks
cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s30: a person who enters or intends to enter a transaction whose principal purpose is a tax advantage must give the information without notice or request (subsection (1)); timing and penalties are left to regulations (subsection (2)). Related: ntaa2025:s47 (counteracting avoidance).
cases.question: A consultant is offering us a scheme to cut our company tax bill. Do we have to tell the tax office about it?

claims.text: A person who enters or intends to enter into a transaction or agreement whose principal purpose is a benefit which enables, or might be expected to enable, that person to obtain a tax advantage shall, without notice or request, give the relevant tax authority information about that transaction or agreement.

"Tax advantage" includes a relief or increased relief from tax, repayment or increased repayment of tax, avoidance or reduction of a charge to tax or an assessment to tax, avoidance of a possible assessment to tax, deferral of a payment of tax or advancement of a repayment of tax, and avoidance of an obligation to deduct or account for tax.
"Transaction" includes a course of action, agreement, scheme or arrangement.

The relevant tax authority may make regulations on the information to be provided, the form and manner of delivery, the period of time within which it shall be provided, and administrative penalties for non-disclosure, false disclosure, incomplete disclosure or late disclosure.

Separately, the relevant tax authority may counteract a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement by adjusting, disregarding or re-characterising it, unless the taxable person proves to the authority's satisfaction that granting the benefit would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Act or any other tax law.

An arrangement is a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement where, having regard to the facts and circumstances, it is reasonable to conclude that its main purpose was to obtain a tax benefit or advantage, that obtaining the advantage is contrary to the object and purpose of the provisions of the Act or any other tax law, that it results directly or indirectly in misuse or abuse of those provisions, or that it lacks commercial substance or coherence in whole or in part.

gaps: Whether the consultant's scheme has a principal purpose of obtaining a tax advantage, and so is a disclosable transaction or agreement, depends on the scheme's details, which are not given.
The regulations on the information, form, deadline and penalties for disclosure are not among the passages.
Whether the scheme would be a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement cannot be decided without its facts.

must_not: claim that the company is a small company
computed amount
cases.rationale: nta2025:s202:def:small-company: turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less and fixed assets not over ₦250,000,000, professional services excluded, so ₦65 million turnover fails the test; the rate is then 30% (nta2025:s56).
cases.question: Our catering company's turnover grew to ₦65 million this year, but our fixed assets are only ₦20 million. Are we still a small company for income tax?

claims.text: A "small company" in the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

Company income tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company at 0% for a small company and at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act for any other company.

The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 separately defines "small business" as a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, and professional services businesses are excluded from that definition too.

gaps: Whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
The comparison of the question's turnover figure with the turnover limit in the small company definition is not done here, as it needs a comparison of figures.
The passages do not say whether the "small business" definition in the Tax Administration Act applies to the question of the income tax rate.

<question>
Our catering company's turnover grew to ₦65 million this year, but our fixed assets are only ₦20 million. Are we still a small company for income tax?
</question>
<gaps>
<gap index="0">
The passages do not say whether the "small business" definition in the Tax Administration Act applies to the question of the income tax rate.
</gap>
</gaps>

cases.rendered:
A "small company" in the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Company income tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company at 0% for a small company and at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act for any other company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 separately defines "small business" as a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, and professional services businesses are excluded from that definition too. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
- The comparison of the question's turnover figure with the turnover limit in the small company definition is not done here, as it needs a comparison of figures.
- The passages do not say whether the "small business" definition in the Tax Administration Act applies to the question of the income tax rate.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)

cases.rationale: An insurance sum for damage or loss of assets is a disposal (nta2025:s35 subsection (2)(b)). nta2025:s43: if applied within three years to a replacement, a chargeable gain arises when compensation plus scrap value exceeds the replacement cost; otherwise an additional asset for capital allowance. The three-year condition is material (D-43(b)).
cases.question: Our warehouse burnt down and the insurer paid us. If we use the money to build a replacement, is any of the payout taxed?

claims.text: Where an asset is lost or destroyed and a capital sum received as compensation is applied within three years of receipt in acquiring another asset in its replacement, the owner is deemed to make a chargeable gain if the compensation together with the residual or scrap value is greater than the cost of the replacement asset.

Where that compensation together with the residual or scrap value is lower than the cost of the replacement asset, the owner is deemed, for the purposes of the First Schedule, to have acquired an additional asset for an amount equal to the cost of the new asset less the compensation together with the residual or scrap value.
Except for that additional asset, allowance claimed on the new asset for the purposes of the First Schedule is limited to the residue of the old asset, if any.
The definition of building includes a warehouse, being a structure permanently affixed to land for all or most of its useful life.

Rights under a policy of insurance, other than one effected in a capital redemption business or industrial assurance business, are not an asset on the disposal of which a chargeable gain may accrue, except as expressly provided under Part VIII.

gaps: The passages do not say that a warehouse is an asset to which section 43 applies, or that building a replacement counts as acquiring another asset in its replacement.
The passages do not say whether the insurer's payment is a capital sum received by way of compensation for the loss or destruction.
The passages do not say what the insurance policy is, so it is unclear whether the exception for capital redemption or industrial assurance business applies.
Comparing the payout plus any residual or scrap value with the cost of the replacement is a calculation that the passages leave to be done on the actual figures.
The passages do not give the rate of tax on a chargeable gain.

A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form, on or before the 21st day of the following month, with or without a notice and whether or not an economic activity has taken place. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The VAT return must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The monthly filing rule in subsection (1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A small business may, by written notice to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption given to small businesses, including registration, charging of tax on taxable supplies and filing of returns. This opt-out does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A business that ceases to be a small business must file monthly VAT returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

When working out whether a person meets the small company threshold, the value of the supply of the person's capital asset is excluded. So is the value of a supply made solely because the person sold the whole or part of its business or permanently stopped carrying on business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Where the Service grants an extension for filing VAT returns, this does not extend the time to pay the tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

- The passages do not define 'small business' or give its turnover threshold, so they do not show whether the bakery is a small business.

- Whether the bakery's goods are taxable supplies is not stated in the passages.

This rule does not apply to franked investment income as provided in the Act.

claims.text: A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria must register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.

Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.

A non-resident person that makes a taxable supply to a person in Nigeria may appoint a representative for the purpose of compliance with its VAT obligations.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

cases.rendered:
For companies, the definition of "connected persons" includes a company that is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

The definition also includes two companies being connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

The definition also includes two companies being connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

A company is also connected to two or more persons who, acting together or through a person acting on their directions, exercise control over the company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions or wishes of the other, or both may reasonably be expected to act that way for a third person, or one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

"Related parties" has the same meaning as connected persons. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "related parties"]

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "related parties" (gazette page A 509)

claims.text: Interest on debt employed in generating the income of a trade, business, profession or vocation is deductible, subject to the provisions of the Third Schedule.

Where a Nigerian company or a permanent establishment of a non-resident company in Nigeria incurs interest or similar expenditure on debt issued by a connected person, the excess interest is a disallowable deduction for the purpose of Chapter Two.

Excess interest means total interest paid or payable to a connected person that is more than 30% of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of the Nigerian company in that accounting period.
The limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company that is engaged in the business of banking or insurance.

Where interest expenditure is not wholly deducted for an assessment year, the part not deducted is carried forward to the following assessment year or years. It is allowed against the profits, if any, of any business carried on by the company and assessable for that year, to the extent permitted under paragraph (2) of the Schedule.
Interest expenditure is not carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed.

For the Schedule, debt means any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges that are deductible in computing income chargeable under the head profits and gains of business or profession.
No deduction is allowed for any payment to a connected person that is not consistent with the Transfer Pricing Regulations issued by the Service.

Interest on debt employed in generating the income of a trade, business, profession or vocation is deductible, subject to the provisions of the Third Schedule. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 20(1)(a) to (h)]

Where a Nigerian company or a permanent establishment of a non-resident company in Nigeria incurs interest or similar expenditure on debt issued by a connected person, the excess interest is a disallowable deduction for the purpose of Chapter Two. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Third Schedule]

Excess interest means total interest paid or payable to a connected person that is more than 30% of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of the Nigerian company in that accounting period. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Third Schedule]

The limit does not apply to a Nigerian subsidiary of a foreign company that is engaged in the business of banking or insurance. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Third Schedule]

Where interest expenditure is not wholly deducted for an assessment year, the part not deducted is carried forward to the following assessment year or years. It is allowed against the profits, if any, of any business carried on by the company and assessable for that year, to the extent permitted under paragraph (2) of the Schedule. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Third Schedule]

Interest expenditure is not carried forward for more than five assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the excess interest expenditure was first computed. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Third Schedule]

My shop's records show almost no profit. Can the tax office tax me on a share of my sales instead?
</question>

cases.rendered:
Where a business produces no assessable profit, or an assessable profit less than expected from that business, or the true amount of the assessable profit cannot be readily ascertained, the relevant tax authority may act under section 38. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 38]

In the case of a resident, the relevant tax authority may assess and charge the taxable person on such fair and reasonable percentage of the gross income from the trade or business as the relevant tax authority may determine. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 38]

In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount resulting from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 38]

For this purpose, profit margin is the proportion of Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. For persons not required to publish financial statements, it is the margin the relevant tax authority ascertains from financial statements of comparative companies. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 38]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the shop owner is a resident or a non-resident is not stated in the question.
- The actual percentage the tax authority would apply is not given in the passages.
- Whether a shop's records showing almost no profit count as profit 'less than expected' is not stated in the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 38 (gazette pages A 283, A 284)

claims.text: Section 192 is about transactions between related parties, which are to be at arm's length.
A company involved in an arrangement with a related party shall ensure that the terms and conditions of the arrangement are at arm's length.
The company shall also report the arrangement in the form and manner prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where, in the opinion of a relevant tax authority, a company has entered into an arrangement with a related party which is not at arm's length, the authority may make necessary adjustments to bring it into line with arm's length terms as provided under the Transfer Pricing Regulations.
The relevant tax authority may make rules or regulations for the administration of section 192.
For section 192, an "arrangement" includes any agreement, understanding, scheme, financial or commercial relation, transaction or series of transactions.
For section 192, "arm's length terms and conditions" means such terms and conditions obtainable if the transaction or arrangement was between unrelated parties dealing in comparative circumstances.

gaps: The Transfer Pricing Regulations, which section 192(2) refers to, are not among the passages.
The meaning of "related party" is not among the passages.

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance in accordance with Part I of the First Schedule. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4)]

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

That 15% rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not define a small company, so whether the company is one cannot be determined.
- The question does not say whether the ₦120 million is total profits after losses and capital allowances, so the taxable amount is not known.
- The question does not give the company's turnover or say whether it is part of an MNE group.
- The tax calculation itself is not done here; it would need the rate that applies and the company's total profits.
- Section 27(6) on losses and Part I of the First Schedule on capital allowances are not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4) (gazette pages A 412, A 413)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4): The National Assembly text requires companies in the priority sector to obtain a certificate of acceptance from the Industrial Inspectorate Department for qualifying capital expenditure; the gazette has no such condition. (DR-039)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)
